sections.section: Second floor · The Botticelli rooms and the Tribune
Second floor · Raphael, Michelangelo and the Niobe Room
First floor · Venice and the Verone

tracks.title: Welcome to the Uffizi
tracks.where: Outside, in the Piazzale degli Uffizi: the long, narrow stone courtyard between the two wings of the building, with statues of famous Tuscans in the niches along the piers and the river at the far end.
tracks.what: The Uffizi building, designed by Giorgio Vasari for Cosimo I de' Medici, built 1560–1580 and completed after 1574 by Francesco I and Bernardo Buontalenti; the gallery's opening to the public on 24 June 1769; the Family Pact of 1737; how the guide works.
tracks.listen: How a block of government offices became one of the world's first public museums, why the collection never left Florence, and how to use the three lengths of this guide.

tracks.title: A2 · The Eastern Corridor
tracks.where: Room A2, the Eastern Corridor, just outside the vestibule at the top of the staircase: a long, bright corridor with tall windows over the courtyard on one side, ancient marble statues and busts along the walls, and a painted ceiling overhead.
tracks.what: Giorgio Vasari's Eastern Corridor, first of the three top-floor corridors (east, south, west), originally conceived as a loggia open onto the Piazzale; the Medici collection of ancient sculpture, including Roman copies of lost Greek works; the grotesque ceiling, first bay painted in 1581 for Grand Duke Francesco I, the other corridors decorated over the next two centuries.
tracks.listen: Why a corridor may have given us the word "gallery", what the statues and the ceiling are, and the one rule for finding every painting room in the museum.

tracks.title: A3 · Painted crosses
tracks.where: Room A3, the first painting room, at the short end of the Eastern Corridor toward Palazzo Vecchio, on the far side of the vestibule from the rest of the route. Look for the big painted cross on a gold ground, nearly three metres tall, with Christ upright and eyes open and small scenes on either side of him.
tracks.what: Pisan painter, Painted cross, 12th century (dating "highly uncertain"), tempera on wood, gold ground, 276 × 231 cm, Uffizi inv. 1890 no. 432; with the other early gold-ground panels of the room.
tracks.listen: The oldest room in the gallery: what a twelfth-century cross was for, why it is painted on gold, and three things to carry into the next room.

tracks.title: A4 · Three Maestàs
tracks.where: Room A4, "Giotto, Cimabue": the large room with three huge altarpieces of the Virgin and Child enthroned on gold, each over three metres tall. Stand in the middle, where you can see all three.
tracks.what: Cimabue, Santa Trinita Maestà, c. 1290–1300, 384 × 223 cm; Duccio di Buoninsegna, Rucellai Madonna, c. 1285, 450 × 290 cm; Giotto, Ognissanti Maestà, c. 1300–1305, 325 × 204 cm; all tempera on wood, gold background. Dante, Purgatorio XI, 94–96 (Longfellow translation).
tracks.listen: Dante's warning about fame, and how to compare three Maestàs painted within about twenty years of one another.

tracks.title: A4 · Cimabue — Santa Trinita Maestà
tracks.where: In Room A4, in front of Cimabue's Maestà: the tall gold panel, nearly four metres high, with eight angels lifting the throne and four prophets standing in arches beneath it.
tracks.what: Cimabue, Virgin and Child Enthroned, and Prophets (Santa Trinita Maestà), c. 1290–1300, tempera on wood, gold background, 384 × 223 cm, Uffizi inv. 1890 no. 8343.
tracks.listen: Why the museum now dates Cimabue's great panel after Duccio's, how to read it from the prophets up, and Vasari's story of the shepherd boy.

tracks.title: A4 · Duccio — Rucellai Madonna
tracks.where: In Room A4, in front of the largest of the three Maestàs, four and a half metres tall: the Virgin on a slender throne held by six kneeling angels, three on each side, with small roundels of saints around the frame.
tracks.what: Duccio di Buoninsegna, Virgin and Child enthroned, surrounded by angels (Rucellai Madonna), c. 1285, tempera on wood, gold background, 450 × 290 cm; on deposit from the church of Santa Maria Novella, Florence.
tracks.listen: The detective story of a painting credited to the wrong man for three centuries, and the line that gives Duccio away.

tracks.title: A4 · Giotto — Ognissanti Maestà
tracks.where: In Room A4, in front of Giotto's Maestà, the smallest of the three at just over three metres: the Virgin seated in a pointed marble tabernacle, with two angels kneeling at her feet holding vases of flowers.
tracks.what: Giotto, Virgin and Child enthroned, surrounded by angels and saints (Ognissanti Maestà), c. 1300–1305, tempera on wood, gold background, 325 × 204 cm, Uffizi inv. 1890 no. 8344.
tracks.listen: How hidden halos and a body with weight changed painting, and why Dante had a point.

tracks.title: A5 · Siena: the Lorenzetti brothers
tracks.where: Room A5, "Lorenzetti, Simone Martini": a room of Sienese gold-ground paintings. Ambrogio's Presentation in the Temple is the tall panel showing a church interior with columns and a starry vault; Pietro's smaller Madonna shows mother and child gazing at each other among angels.
tracks.what: Ambrogio Lorenzetti, Presentation at the Temple, 1342, tempera on wood, gold background, 257 × 168 cm, inv. 1890 no. 8346; Pietro Lorenzetti, Virgin and Child enthroned, with angels, c. 1340, tempera on panel, 145 × 122 cm, inv. 1890 no. 445.
tracks.listen: Siena's answer to Florence, two brothers who probably died in the Black Death, and two tiny human details in the gold.

tracks.title: A5 · Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi — Annunciation
tracks.where: In Room A5, in front of the great gold Annunciation, nearly two metres high: the angel kneeling on one side, the Virgin drawing back on the other, a vase of lilies between them and words in raised gold running across the gold ground, with a standing saint in each side panel.
tracks.what: Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi, Annunciation with St. Maxima and St. Ansanus, 1333, tempera on wood, gold background, 184 × 168 cm, Uffizi inv. 1890 nos. 451, 452, 453.
tracks.listen: A painting that writes a voice across the air, a frightened young woman inside the gold, and two brothers-in-law who signed it together.

tracks.title: A6 · Extra · Florence in the fourteenth century
tracks.where: Room A6, "14th Century", through the doorway at the back of Room A5. Look for Pietro Lorenzetti's tall gold altarpiece of a nun in a dark habit, full length in the centre, surrounded by small story scenes.
tracks.what: Pietro Lorenzetti, Saint Humility and scenes from her life, c. 1335–1340, tempera on wood, gold background, 257 × 168 cm, inv. 1890 nn. 6120–6126, 6129–6131, 8347. Not on display (restoration, no return date): Giovanni da Milano, Ognissanti Polyptych, and Giottino, Pietà di San Remigio.
tracks.listen: A Sienese painting of a Florentine founder, the nuns who carried it through a siege, and two works that are away for now.

tracks.title: A7 · Lorenzo Monaco — Coronation of the Virgin
tracks.where: Room A7, "Lorenzo Monaco, Gentile da Fabriano". Lorenzo Monaco's Coronation is the huge gold altarpiece, four and a half metres high, with Christ crowning the Virgin above a striped, starry rainbow and two saints in white kneeling at the sides.
tracks.what: Lorenzo Monaco, Coronation of the Virgin, 1414 (inscribed February 1413, Florentine calendar), tempera on wood, gold background, 450 × 350 cm, inv. 1890 n. 885. Also in the room: Gentile da Fabriano, Adoration of the Magi, 1423.
tracks.listen: What International Gothic means, a monk who painted for his own abbey, and a date that is a year out.

tracks.title: A7 · Gentile da Fabriano — Adoration of the Magi
tracks.where: In Room A7, in front of the great gold Adoration, three metres high and almost as wide, under a frame of three pointed arches: a long procession of kings, horses and animals winding down to the Holy Family on the left, with a row of small scenes along the base.
tracks.what: Gentile da Fabriano, Adoration of the Magi, signed and dated May 1423, tempera on wood, 300 × 282 cm, Uffizi inv. 1890 n. 8364; the predella Presentation in the Temple is a modern copy of the original in the Louvre.
tracks.listen: How to read the most lavish painting of International Gothic like a story, the metal that stands up from the surface, and the copy hidden in plain sight.

tracks.title: A8 · Masolino, Masaccio and Fra Angelico
tracks.where: Room A8, "Masaccio, Beato Angelico, P. Uccello". The Saint Anne is the gold panel with Saint Anne seated high behind the Virgin, who holds the Child on her lap; Uccello's wide battle scene is also in this room.
tracks.what: Masolino and Masaccio, Saint Anne, Madonna and Child, five angels ("Sant'Anna Metterza"), c. 1424–1425, tempera on wood, 175 × 103 cm, inv. 1890 no. 8386; Fra Angelico, Glorification of Mary, 1431–1435, with its predella, inv. 1890 no. 1612; Fra Angelico, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Angels, 1435, from Pontassieve, Deposits no. 143.
tracks.listen: Two painters called Tommaso, a Child built like Hercules, Fra Angelico's crowded heaven, and Uccello's love of perspective.

tracks.title: A8 · Paolo Uccello — The Battle of San Romano
tracks.where: In Room A8, in front of the wide battle panel, more than three metres across: armoured horsemen, a thicket of raised and broken lances, fallen soldiers on the ground and small orange trees filling the top corners.
tracks.what: Paolo Uccello, Battle of San Romano, c. 1435–1440, tempera on wood, 182 × 323 cm, Uffizi inv. 1890 n. 479, signed "PAULI UGIELI OPUS"; the central panel of a set of three, with the others in the National Gallery, London, and the Louvre, Paris.
tracks.listen: How the Medici turned someone else's battle pictures into their own, and how Uccello lets the lances tell you who wins.

tracks.section: Second floor · The Botticelli rooms and the Tribune
tracks.title: Botticelli rooms · Pollaiolo and Botticelli — Fortitude
tracks.where: In the first of the Botticelli rooms, the room of painted Virtues: a row of seated women in tall gilded frames along one wall. Botticelli's Fortitude is the young woman wearing armour over her dress, with a sceptre in her hand.
tracks.what: Sandro Botticelli, Fortitude, 1470, tempera grassa on poplar, 167 × 87 cm, inv. 1890 n. 1606; with Piero del Pollaiolo's Virtues for the Tribunale di Mercanzia, among them Charity, 1469–1470, tempera grassa on wood, 168 × 90.5 cm, inv. 1890 no. 499; also in the room, Portrait of a Lady, attributed to Piero del Pollaiolo, c. 1475–1480.
tracks.listen: Botticelli's first documented work, the commission he was never meant to get, and how the newly rehung Botticelli rooms run.

tracks.section: Second floor · The Botticelli rooms and the Tribune
tracks.title: Botticelli rooms · Extra · Botticelli — Adoration of the Magi
tracks.where: In the Botticelli rooms, in front of the Adoration of the Magi, a panel just over a metre across: the Holy Family raised up at the centre, with a crowd of richly dressed Florentines gathered on either side. It opens the Botticelli sequence after the room of Virtues.
tracks.what: Sandro Botticelli, Adoration of the Magi (the Del Lama altarpiece), 1470–1475, tempera grassa on wood, 111 × 137 cm, inv. 1890 no. 882.
tracks.listen: A patron who painted himself in and then fell into disgrace, the Medici as kings, and a young man who may be Botticelli looking straight at you.

tracks.section: Second floor · The Botticelli rooms and the Tribune
tracks.title: Botticelli rooms · Botticelli — Primavera
tracks.where: In the Botticelli rooms, in front of the Primavera: a wide, dark panel over three metres across, nine figures in a grove of orange trees on a meadow of flowers, with Venus at the centre. A round Madonna hangs on each side, and the Birth of Venus faces it across the passage.
tracks.what: Sandro Botticelli, Spring (Primavera), c. 1480, tempera grassa on poplar, 207 × 319 cm, Uffizi inv. 1890 n. 8360; flanked by the Madonna of the Rose Garden and the Madonna of the Cherubim.
tracks.listen: How to read the Primavera from right to left, the forty-two plants under their feet, and why its meaning is still a mystery.

tracks.section: Second floor · The Botticelli rooms and the Tribune
tracks.title: Botticelli rooms · Botticelli — The Birth of Venus
tracks.where: In the Botticelli rooms, in front of the Birth of Venus, facing the Primavera across the passage: a wide, pale canvas almost three metres across, the goddess standing on a scallop shell between the winds on the left and a woman holding out a flowered cloak on the right. A round Madonna hangs on each side.
tracks.what: Sandro Botticelli, Birth of Venus, c. 1485, tempera on canvas, 172.5 × 278.5 cm, Uffizi inv. 1890 n. 878; flanked by the Madonna of the Magnificat and the Madonna of the Pomegranate.
tracks.listen: Who is who around Venus, what Botticelli borrowed from Lorenzo the Magnificent's gem, and why the surface looks so pale.

tracks.section: Second floor · The Botticelli rooms and the Tribune
tracks.title: Botticelli rooms · Extra · Magnificat, Pomegranate and Calumny
tracks.where: In the Venus room of the Botticelli rooms. The Madonna of the Magnificat is the large round painting beside the Venus, with Mary writing in a book; the Madonna of the Pomegranate is the round painting on the Venus's other side. The Calumny is a small, crowded panel, under a metre wide, of figures in a marble hall by the sea.
tracks.what: Sandro Botticelli, Virgin and Child, and Angels (Madonna of the Magnificat), c. 1483, tempera on wood, diameter 118 cm, inv. 1890 n. 1609; Madonna of the Pomegranate (named in the June 2026 news; no page read); Calumny of Apelles, c. 1495, tempera on wood, 62 × 91 cm, inv. 1890 no. 1496.
tracks.listen: A Madonna writing her own hymn, and the dark little allegory that closes Botticelli's story.

tracks.section: Second floor · The Botticelli rooms and the Tribune
tracks.title: A13 · Hugo van der Goes — The Portinari Triptych
tracks.where: Room A13, "Hugo van der Goes". Stand back from the one enormous three-part altarpiece that fills the room, more than six metres wide when open: a newborn Child on the bare ground at the centre, a kneeling family with towering saints on the wings, and a vase of flowers at the front.
tracks.what: Hugo van der Goes, Adoration of the Shepherds with angels and Saint Thomas, Saint Anthony, Saint Margaret, Mary Magdalen and the Portinari family (recto); Annunciation (verso), known as the Portinari Triptych, c. 1477–1478, oil on wood, 274 × 652 cm open, 1890 nn. 3191, 3192, 3193.
tracks.listen: How a banker's altarpiece from Bruges crossed the sea to Florence, and what the city's painters saw in it.

tracks.section: Second floor · The Botticelli rooms and the Tribune
tracks.title: A14 · Extra · Maps and mathematics
tracks.where: Room A14, the Room of the Maps, off Room A13: walls painted with large maps of Tuscany and its coast, with place names in gold, under a dark coffered ceiling. Room A15, the small Room of Mathematics, is between Room A13 and the Tribune.
tracks.what: Room A14, Terrazzo delle Carte geografiche: maps painted by Ludovico Buti from Stefano Bonsignori's survey, coffered ceiling by Jacopo Zucchi brought from Rome, for Ferdinando I. Room A15, Stanzino delle Matematiche: ceiling frescoed by Giulio Parigi, 1599–1600; restored 2025; small bronzes in the niches. DATED: Willem Tetrode, Venus, bronze, on loan to Oxford until 11 Apr 2027.
tracks.listen: A cardinal who brought his ceiling home from Rome, and a small room that celebrated Archimedes.

tracks.section: Second floor · The Botticelli rooms and the Tribune
tracks.title: A16 · The Tribune
tracks.where: At a doorway of the Tribune, Room A16: a small octagonal room with red velvet walls, a dome shining with mother-of-pearl and a floor of coloured marble. The life-size marble goddess covering herself with her hands is the Medici Venus.
tracks.what: Bernardo Buontalenti, the Tribune, 1581–1583, for Francesco I de' Medici. Medici Venus, Hellenistic art, late 2nd – early 1st century BC, Parian marble, h. 153 cm, 1914 no. 224. Also: Wrestlers, Roman art, Parian marble, 1914 no. 216; Knife Grinder (the Scythian), Roman art, 2nd century AD, 1914 no. 230.
tracks.listen: A treasure room built as a model of the universe, and the goddess who was taken to Paris and came back.

tracks.title: A23 · The Southern Corridor
tracks.where: The short Southern Corridor, Room A23, at the river end of the building. Go to the tall windows: the Arno is below, with the Ponte Vecchio along the river. A red porphyry she-wolf stands in the middle of the corridor.
tracks.what: The South Corridor (or Second Corridor), ceiling frescoes 1696–1699 for Cosimo III; ancient sculpture including the so-called Dying Alexander (a Greek original head, 2nd century BC), a porphyry she-wolf (2nd century AD) and a Muse signed by Atticus of Aphrodisias (late 4th century AD). View of the Arno, the Ponte Vecchio and the Vasari Corridor.
tracks.listen: The view of the river and the bridge, the Medici's private passage over it, and the night in 1966 when the river came into the city.

tracks.title: A25 · Domenico Veneziano — Santa Lucia altarpiece
tracks.where: Room A25, "Domenico Veneziano, Piero della Francesca". Stand in front of the big, almost square altarpiece, about two metres each way: the Virgin and Child enthroned under a light, pink and green marble loggia, with two saints on each side and orange trees above.
tracks.what: Domenico Veneziano, Madonna and Child enthroned with St. Francis, John the Baptist, St. Zenobius and St. Lucy (Santa Lucia de' Magnoli Altarpiece), c. 1445, tempera on wood, 209 × 213 cm, 1890 n. 884; restored 2024 by the Opificio delle Pietre Dure.
tracks.listen: A painter from Venice who filled an altarpiece with daylight, and the murder Vasari invented for him.

tracks.title: A25 · Piero della Francesca — The Duke and Duchess of Urbino
tracks.where: Room A25. Stand in front of the two small panels in one frame, each about the size of a large book: a pale woman on the left and a man in a red cap on the right, facing each other in strict profile, with one wide landscape running behind them both.
tracks.what: Piero della Francesca, The Duke and Duchess of Urbino Federico da Montefeltro and Battista Sforza, c. 1473–1475, oil on wood, 47 × 33 cm each, 1890 nn. 1615, 3342; reverses painted with triumphs, the Virtues and Latin inscriptions.
tracks.listen: Why the most famous couple in the Renaissance face each other without a flicker of feeling, and why she is so pale.

tracks.title: A27 · Perugino
tracks.where: Room A27, "Pietro Perugino". Two big, almost square altarpieces, each about one and three-quarter metres across: the Pietà, with the dead Christ held by his mother under a grey stone portico, and the Oration in the Garden, with Christ kneeling on a rock and three apostles asleep below.
tracks.what: Perugino (Pietro di Cristoforo Vannucci), Pietà, c. 1493–1496, oil on wood, 168 × 176 cm, 1890 no. 8365; and Oration in the Garden, c. 1493–1496, oil on wood, 166 × 171 cm, 1890 n. 8367; both painted for San Giusto alle Mura, Florence.
tracks.listen: The best-paid painter of his day, the church that vanished, and the calm that Raphael learned.

tracks.title: A28 · Filippino Lippi and Piero di Cosimo
tracks.where: Room A28, "Filippino Lippi, Piero di Cosimo". The big, almost square Adoration of the Magi, about two and a half metres high, crowded with kings and horsemen; and nearby a long, low panel of a sea monster, a hero in the sky and a crowd on the shore.
tracks.what: Filippino Lippi, Adoration of the Magi, 1496, tempera grassa on wood, 258 × 243 cm, 1890 n. 1566. Piero di Cosimo, Perseus frees Andromeda, 1510–1515, tempera grassa on wood, 70 × 120 cm, 1890 no. 1536.
tracks.listen: The painting that replaced Leonardo's unfinished one, a Medici in yellow with an astrolabe, and the strangest painter in Florence.

tracks.title: A31 · Extra · Luca Signorelli
tracks.where: Room A31, "Luca Signorelli". The large round painting, about one and a quarter metres across: the Virgin in a wide red robe reading a book, with the Child and Joseph pressed close. A second Signorelli Madonna, with small nude figures in the background, is in the next room, Room A32.
tracks.what: Luca Signorelli, Holy Family, c. 1487–1488, oil on wood, diameter 124 cm, 1890 n. 1605, Room A31. Also: Luca Signorelli, Madonna with Child, c. 1490, oil on wood, 170 × 115 cm, 1890 n. 502, Room A32.
tracks.listen: How a painter from Cortona showed Michelangelo the way, twice.

tracks.title: A35 · Leonardo: the Baptism
tracks.where: Room A35, "Leonardo Da Vinci". Stand in front of the tall panel, almost two metres high, of John the Baptist pouring water over Christ, who stands in a shallow river; two angels kneel on the bank at the left.
tracks.what: Andrea del Verrocchio and Leonardo da Vinci, The Baptism of Christ, c. 1470–1475, tempera and oil on panel, 177 × 151 cm, 1890 n. 8358.
tracks.listen: A workshop picture in which a young assistant may have painted far more than one angel.

tracks.title: A35 · Leonardo — Annunciation
tracks.where: Room A35. Stand in front of the long, low panel, more than two metres wide and less than one high: the angel kneels on a flowery lawn at the left, the Virgin sits at a carved marble lectern at the right, and dark trees and a misty distance open between them.
tracks.what: Leonardo da Vinci, Annunciation, c. 1472, oil on wood, 90 × 222 cm, 1890 n. 1618; at the Uffizi since 1867, from San Bartolomeo a Monteoliveto.
tracks.listen: A painting nobody can trace to its first church, made by a young man already looking harder than anyone around him.

tracks.title: A35 · Leonardo — Adoration of the Magi
tracks.where: Room A35. Stand back from the big, almost square panel, nearly two and a half metres each way, drawn and painted mostly in browns: the Virgin and Child at the centre, a crowd swirling round them, ruins with two staircases on the left and horsemen fighting behind.
tracks.what: Leonardo da Vinci, Adoration of the Magi (San Donato in Scopeto), c. 1482, drawing in charcoal, watercolour ink and oil on wood, 244 × 240 cm, 1890 n. 1594; restored at the Opificio delle Pietre Dure, 2011–2017.
tracks.listen: The painting Leonardo walked away from, and what five years of cleaning found hidden in it.

tracks.section: Second floor · Raphael, Michelangelo and the Niobe Room
tracks.title: A37 · Extra · The Cabinet of Marbles
tracks.where: Room A37, the Cabinet of Marbles, beside the top of the Buontalenti staircase: a deep red room with ancient reliefs set into the walls. Look for the marble boy, a little under a metre tall, sitting on a rock and pulling a thorn from his foot.
tracks.what: Boy with Thorn, also known as Spinario, 1st century BC, Greek marble with additions in Carrara marble, h. 84 cm. Room rearranged in July 2024: twelve Roman reliefs back in their original places, and other ancient marbles.
tracks.listen: A terrace that became a sculpture room, and a boy who has been busy with his foot for two thousand years.

tracks.section: Second floor · Raphael, Michelangelo and the Niobe Room
tracks.title: A38 · Raphael and Michelangelo
tracks.where: Room A38, "Raphael and Michelangelo". Michelangelo's round Holy Family in its carved gold frame is the work to find first; Raphael's Madonna of the Goldfinch and his large canvas of the boy Saint John in a cave, in a leopard skin, are in the same room, with two tiny panels by Fra Bartolomeo.
tracks.what: Overview of Room A38. Raphael, St John the Baptist as a Boy, c. 1518, oil on canvas, 163 × 147 cm. Fra Bartolomeo, Adoration of the Child and Presentation in the Temple, c. 1497, oil on wood, about 20 × 9 cm each, 1890 no. 1477. Also the Doni Tondo (034) and the Madonna of the Goldfinch (035).
tracks.listen: Two rivals in one room, and two smaller works that are easy to miss.

tracks.section: Second floor · Raphael, Michelangelo and the Niobe Room
tracks.title: A38 · Michelangelo — The Doni Tondo
tracks.where: Room A38. Stand in front of the round painting, 120 centimetres across, in its deep carved and gilded frame: Mary twisting round to take the Child from Joseph, in hard bright colours, with a row of nude young men behind a low wall.
tracks.what: Michelangelo Buonarroti, Holy Family, known as the "Doni Tondo", about 1505–1507 (page: 1505–1506), tempera grassa on wood, diameter 120 cm, 1890 n. 1456; frame carved by Francesco del Tasso, probably to Michelangelo's design.
tracks.listen: A sculptor's painting for a merchant's family, the ancient statue hidden in it, and the bride's emblem hidden in the frame.

tracks.section: Second floor · Raphael, Michelangelo and the Niobe Room
tracks.title: A38 · Raphael — Madonna of the Goldfinch
tracks.where: Room A38. Stand in front of the upright panel, about a metre high: the Virgin in red and blue, seated in a soft landscape with a small book, and two little boys at her knees, one holding out a tiny bird to the other.
tracks.what: Raphael, Mary, Christ and the young John the Baptist, known as the "Madonna of the Goldfinch", before February 1506, oil on wood, 107 × 77.2 cm, 1890 n. 1447.
tracks.listen: A wedding present, a landslide that broke it into seventeen pieces, and the small bird that carries the whole story.

tracks.section: Second floor · Raphael, Michelangelo and the Niobe Room
tracks.title: A39 · The Niobe Room
tracks.where: Room A39, the Niobe Room: a long white and gold hall with a coffered ceiling, lined with marble statues of young people running, falling and looking up. Find the tallest group, more than two metres high: a mother pulling her small daughter close.
tracks.what: The Niobe Room, inaugurated 20 Feb 1780, architects Zanobi del Rosso and Gaspare Maria Paoletti. The Niobids, Roman marbles of the 2nd century AD after a celebrated Greek group, found in Rome in 1583. Niobe with her younger daughter, first half of the 2nd century AD, Pentelic marble, h. 228 cm, 1914 no. 294.
tracks.listen: A myth about a mother's pride, statues that travelled from a Roman vineyard, and the night in 1993 when this room was hit.

tracks.section: Second floor · Raphael, Michelangelo and the Niobe Room
tracks.title: A24 · Down the Lanzi staircase
tracks.where: The far end of the Western Corridor, Room A24, at the top of the Lanzi staircase, before you go down. The panoramic terrace is at this end of the floor too.
tracks.what: The Western Corridor (Third Corridor), ancient statues in facing pairs, ceilings painted over the two centuries after the first bay of 1581; the Lanzi staircase down to the first floor; the panoramic terrace with the café, second floor.
tracks.listen: The most important direction in the guide: one floor down, not out to the street.

tracks.title: B2 · The Contini Bonacossi collection
tracks.where: Room B2, at the near end of the long hall of the Contini Bonacossi collection, Room B1, on the side away from the Info Point, beside Room B4. Stand in front of the big, square gold altarpiece, about two and a half metres each way, of the Virgin enthroned with angels and saints. The tall fresco of another enthroned Madonna, with two children offering flowers, is in the same room.
tracks.what: Stefano di Giovanni, known as Sassetta, Madonna of the Snow Altarpiece, 1432, tempera on panel, 240 × 256 cm, Contini Bonacossi no. 1. Also: Andrea del Castagno, Madonna and Child enthroned with Saints Jerome and John the Baptist, two angels, and two children from the Pazzi family, c. 1449–1450, detached fresco, 290 × 212 cm, Contini Bonacossi no. 2.
tracks.listen: A private collection inside the museum, an altarpiece with an angel making a snowball, and a fresco cut from a castle wall.

tracks.title: B4 · Giovanni Bellini — Saint Jerome in the Desert
tracks.where: Room B4, "Giovanni Bellini". Stand in front of the larger of the two Saint Jeromes: a tall panel, about one and a half metres high, of an old saint reading on a rocky ledge, a lion in its den and a walled city in the distance. Cima da Conegliano's Saint Jerome in the same room is tiny, about a third of a metre high, with a skull at its centre.
tracks.what: Giovanni Bellini, St. Jerome in the Desert, c. 1480, oil on panel, 151.7 × 113.7 cm, Contini Bonacossi no. 25. Also: Giovanni Battista Cima da Conegliano, St. Jerome in the Desert, c. 1510–1520, oil on panel, 33 × 27.5 cm, Contini Bonacossi no. 19, same room.
tracks.listen: A desert hermit, a lizard with a meaning, and a city that never existed, built from real buildings Bellini had seen.

tracks.title: B5 · Extra · Bramantino — Madonna and Child with eight saints
tracks.where: Room B5, "Bramantino", across the hall from Room B4. The large altarpiece, about two metres tall: the Virgin and Child seated on steps under a loggia of columns, with men gathered around them and sky-blue drapery echoing the sky.
tracks.what: Bartolomeo Suardi, known as Bramantino, Madonna and Child with eight saints, catalogue date c. 1512–1514, oil on panel, 205 × 166.5 cm, Contini Bonacossi no. 3.
tracks.listen: A painter named after his teacher, and a crowd of saints that includes a poor man and perhaps the patron himself.

tracks.title: B8 · Bernini — Saint Lawrence
tracks.where: Room B8, "Bernini", at the far end of the Contini Bonacossi hall. The white marble saint lies stretched out, about a metre long, on a carved wooden base shaped like a tree wrapped in flames.
tracks.what: Gian Lorenzo Bernini, Saint Lawrence, 1617, white marble with a carved wooden base, 66 × 108 cm, Contini Bonacossi Collection, room B8.
tracks.listen: A teenage sculptor, a story of a leg held near hot coals, and a face that is not in agony at all.

tracks.title: C1 · The self-portraits
tracks.where: Room C1, "From the origins to the 17th century", the long room beside the foot of the Lanzi staircase. Stand near the seated marble statue of a cardinal in lace, about 1.6 metres high, twisting in his chair near the entrance. Raphael's small self-portrait, a young man in a dark cap and dark clothes, hangs in this room.
tracks.what: Giovan Battista Foggini, Cardinal Leopoldo de' Medici, 1697, marble, 160 cm high, inv. 1914 no. 350. Also: Raphael, Self portrait, 1506, oil on panel, 47.3 × 34.8 cm, inv. 1890 n. 1706, room C1.
tracks.listen: How a cardinal's hobby became the world's great collection of self-portraits, where it hid for decades, and the young Raphael looking back at you.

tracks.title: C2 · Extra · Bill Viola — Self portrait, Submerged
tracks.where: Room C2, "Water and Light". Look for the tall vertical screen showing a man lying on a riverbed with his eyes closed while water flows over him, in slow motion.
tracks.what: Bill Viola, Self portrait – Submerged, 2013, high-definition video on a vertical plasma screen with stereo sound, about 11 minutes in slow motion, 121.2 × 72.4 × 9 cm, inv. 1890 no. 10644.
tracks.listen: A childhood accident in a lake, remembered not as terror but as beauty, and turned into a self-portrait made of water and time.

tracks.title: C3 · Extra · Painters at work
tracks.where: Room C3, "17th century". Look for a small canvas, about half a metre high, of a painter at his easel in a bare studio, with an old bare-chested man kneeling at a lectern in front of him and a brazier of coals on the floor.
tracks.what: Michelangelo Cerquozzi, Self-portrait in his studio, c. 1640–1646, oil on canvas, 51 × 42.5 cm, inv. 1890 n. 10721. Rooms C3 "17th century", C4 "Showing the Artwork", C5 "Early 18th century".
tracks.listen: A painter's studio in seventeenth-century Rome, a model posing as a saint, and a nickname written on the back of the canvas.

tracks.title: D4 · Correggio and Parmigianino
tracks.where: Room D4, "Correggio and Parmigianino", one of the two rooms at the back of Room D1. Stand where you can see the whole of the tallest panel in the room, over two metres high: a pale, elongated Virgin with a large sleeping Child on her lap, a crowd of angels on one side and a single column rising on the other.
tracks.what: Room D4. Parmigianino (Francesco Mazzola), Madonna and Child with Angels (Madonna with the long neck), 1534–1540, oil on panel, 216.5 × 132.5 cm, Palatina n. 230. On loan: Correggio, Adoration of the Christ Child, 1518–1520, oil on canvas, 81 × 77 cm, 1890 no. 1453, in Dresden until 10 Jan 2027 (cuttable sentence). Passing D1, "The 16th century in Lombardia", and D2, "Dosso Dossi and his circle".
tracks.listen: Two painters of Parma, one of them named after the city, and a grand prince who paid for an unfinished picture and called it worthy of Raphael.

tracks.title: D4 · Parmigianino — Madonna with the Long Neck
tracks.where: Room D4, "Correggio and Parmigianino", reached through Room D1. Stand in front of the tallest panel, over two metres high: a pale Virgin with a very long neck, a large sleeping Child across her lap, angels crowding in on the left, and on the right a single column with a tiny figure at its foot.
tracks.what: Parmigianino (Francesco Mazzola), Madonna and Child with Angels (Madonna with the long neck), 1534–1540, oil on panel, 216.5 × 132.5 cm, Palatina n. 230.
tracks.listen: A five-month deadline that became six years, an apology painted on a column, and the saint of whom only one foot exists.

tracks.title: D5 · Extra · Ferrara, Bologna and Rome
tracks.where: Rooms D5 to D8, the group of rooms reached from Room D6 on the corridor. Start in D5, "Painters from Ferrara", at Garofalo's small Annunciation, about three quarters of a metre wide: the angel on the left with a stem of three lilies, the Virgin turning on the right.
tracks.what: D5: Garofalo, Annunciation, c. 1535, oil on wood, 55.2 × 76 cm. D6: "The 16th century in Bologna". D7, "Sebastiano del Piombo and the influence of Michelangelo in Rome": Giulio Romano, Virgin and Child, 1520–1522, oil on panel, 105 × 77 cm; Perin del Vaga, Virgin and Child, c. 1535–1540, oil on canvas, 121 × 91 cm. D8, "Daniele da Volterra - Francesco Salviati": Salviati, Charity, c. 1545, oil on panel, 156 × 122 cm.
tracks.listen: What happened to Raphael's style after his death, carried by his pupils from Rome across Italy, in four small rooms.

tracks.title: D12 · Pontormo and Rosso
tracks.where: Room D12, "Pontormo - Rosso Fiorentino", opening off the short D9 passage. Stand in front of Rosso's altarpiece, about 1.7 metres high: the Virgin and Child enthroned, a gaunt, scowling Saint Jerome and three other saints around them, and two small child angels reading on the steps of the throne.
tracks.what: Room D12. Rosso Fiorentino, Enthroned Madonna and Child with four saints, 1518, oil on panel, 172 × 141 cm, inv. 1890 n. 3190. On loan: Pontormo, Supper at Emmaus, Madonna with Child and the young Saint John, and Portrait of Maria Salviati, at the Scuderie del Quirinale, Rome, until 7 Feb 2027 (cuttable sentence).
tracks.listen: Two young rebels from the same workshop, a patron who said the saints looked like devils, and a painter who took him to court.

tracks.title: D12 · Rosso Fiorentino — Moses Defends the Daughters of Jethro
tracks.where: Room D12, "Pontormo - Rosso Fiorentino". Look for a canvas about 1.6 metres high packed with naked, struggling men in the foreground, bodies flung across one another, and a young woman standing behind them.
tracks.what: Rosso Fiorentino, Moses Defends the Daughters of Jethro, 1523–1527, oil on canvas, 160 × 117 cm, inv. 1890 n. 2151.
tracks.listen: A biblical brawl painted for an enemy of the Medici, sent to a French king, and brought home again to a Medici prince.

tracks.title: D12 · Extra · Rosso Fiorentino — Angel Playing the Lute
tracks.where: Room D12, "Pontormo - Rosso Fiorentino". A small panel, under half a metre across, against a dark background: a child angel with red and white wings bent over a large lute. It is the room's picture on the museum's map.
tracks.what: Rosso Fiorentino, Angel playing the lute, 1521, oil on wood panel, 39.5 × 47 cm, inv. 1890 no. 1505, inscribed "R(u)beus florentini fe(cit?) MDXXI".
tracks.listen: A famous little angel turns out to be a fragment, and the big picture he came from is lost.

tracks.title: D14 · Bronzino's Panciatichi portraits
tracks.where: Room D14, "Bronzino", on the corridor. Find the two matching portraits, each about a metre high: a woman in a deep red gown seated in a dark room, with a gold chain and a book on her lap, and a red-bearded man in black standing at a balustrade in front of city buildings, with a small black puppy at his feet.
tracks.what: Bronzino, Portrait of Lucrezia Panciatichi, 1541–1545, oil on wood, 102 × 83.2 cm, inv. 1890 n. 736; Portrait of Bartolomeo Panciatichi, 1541–1545, oil on wood, 104 × 85 cm, inv. 1890 n. 741; Holy Family with young Saint John (Madonna Panciatichi), 1539–1540, oil on wood, 116.9 × 89.7 cm, inv. 1890 n. 8377. On loan: Pygmalion and Galatea, Scuderie del Quirinale, Rome, until 7 Feb 2027 (cuttable sentence).
tracks.listen: A husband and wife painted by the duke's court painter, a love message on a gold chain, and the secret that put them on trial.

tracks.title: D15 · Bronzino — Eleonora di Toledo with her son Giovanni
tracks.where: Room D15, the Room of the Dynasties, on the corridor next to Room D14. Look for the portrait about 1.15 metres high of a seated woman in a white and gold brocade gown against an intense blue background, her hand resting on the shoulder of a small boy. It is the room's picture on the museum's map.
tracks.what: Bronzino, Portrait of Eleonora di Toledo with her son Giovanni, c. 1545, oil on wood, 115 × 96 cm, inv. 1890 no. 748.
tracks.listen: A duchess who ran the state, a gown that tells the world she will give the family heirs, and a legend about her burial that is not true.

tracks.title: D15 · Extra · Titian's Duke and Duchess of Urbino
tracks.where: Room D15, the Room of the Dynasties. Find Titian's pair of portraits, each just over a metre high: a commander in polished armour against crimson velvet, with batons and a dragon-crested helmet on a shelf behind him, and a seated duchess with a small dog beside her. Barocci's young duke in armour, his hand on a plumed helmet, is in the same room.
tracks.what: Titian, Portrait of Francesco Maria della Rovere, c. 1537, oil on canvas, 114 × 103 cm, inv. 1890 n. 926; Titian, Portrait of Eleonora Gonzaga, Duchess of Urbino, c. 1537, oil on canvas, 114 × 103 cm, inv. 1890 no. 919. Also: Federico Barocci, Portrait of Francesco Maria II della Rovere, Duke of Urbino, 1572, oil on canvas, 113 × 93 cm, inv. 1890 n. 1438. All D15.
tracks.listen: A duke who lent Titian his armour, a duchess painted as the faithful wife, and the son who bought the Venus of Urbino.

tracks.title: D16 · Extra · The Counter-Reformation rooms
tracks.where: Room D16, the Room of the Pillar, through the doorway in the back wall of Room D15 nearer Room D14 (the first counting from D14). Rooms D17, "Classic tradition", and D18, "Room of the Counter-Reformation", open beyond it. In D17, look for two small, jewel-like pictures: Allori's Hercules among nine Muses, painted on copper, and Ligozzi's winged Fortune standing on a globe.
tracks.what: Rooms D16 "Room of the Pillar", D17 "Classic tradition", D18 "Room of the Counter-Reformation". In D17: Alessandro Allori, Hercules crowned by the Muses, 1568, oil on copper, 40 × 29.5 cm, inv. 1890 n. 1544; Jacopo Ligozzi, Allegory of Fortune, 1580–1599, oil on wood, 44 × 26.5 cm, inv. 1890 n. 8023.
tracks.listen: What the Church asked of painters after the Council of Trent, and the private, clever pictures the Medici court kept for itself.

tracks.title: D19 · The Vasari Corridor door
tracks.where: Room D19, "Vasari Corridor entrance", the narrow room through the second doorway in the back wall of Room D15, counting from Room D14. Look for the sign for the Vasari Corridor meeting point. Stay in the room: this guide does not go through the Corridor door.
tracks.what: Room D19, the Vasari Corridor entrance and meeting point. The Vasari Corridor, 1565, about 750 metres, from the Uffizi over the Ponte Vecchio to the Pitti Palace and the Boboli Gardens.
tracks.listen: A private walkway built in five months for a Medici wedding, where the self-portraits once hid, and how it is visited today.

tracks.section: First floor · Venice and the Verone
tracks.title: D20 · The Venetian Chapel and El Greco
tracks.where: Room D20, the Venetian Chapel, the small room off the narrow Vasari Corridor room, D19. Look for a small panel, about two-thirds of a metre high, of a kneeling woman bathing in a garden ringed by a fortified wall, with Latin words on painted scrolls. Titian's portrait of a churchman holding a letter is in the same room.
tracks.what: Lorenzo Lotto, Susanna and the Elders, 1517, oil on panel, 66 × 50 cm, inv. 1890 n. 9491. Also: Titian, Portrait of Bishop of Bologna, Ludovico Beccadelli, 1552, oil on canvas, 117.5 × 97 cm (D20), and El Greco, Saint John the Evangelist and Saint Francis, 1600, oil on canvas, 110 × 86.5 cm (D21).
tracks.listen: A painting where the people talk, a portrait that dates itself, and El Greco's cup of poison, as you cross from Florentine line into Venetian colour.

tracks.section: First floor · Venice and the Verone
tracks.title: D23 · Titian — Venus of Urbino
tracks.where: Room D23, Titian – Venus of Urbino. Stand in front of the wide canvas, about one and two-thirds metres across, of a nude woman reclining on white sheets and looking straight out at you, a little dog asleep at her feet and two maids at a chest in the background.
tracks.what: Titian, Venus of Urbino, 1538, oil on canvas, 119 × 165 cm, inv. 1890 no. 1437 (page "D22" in the old numbering = map D23).
tracks.listen: A painting bought as "the naked woman", a wedding ritual turned into a goddess, and why it once hung beside the Medici Venus.

tracks.section: First floor · Venice and the Verone
tracks.title: D23 · Extra · Titian — Flora
tracks.where: Room D23, near the Venus of Urbino. Look for a smaller canvas, about 80 centimetres high, of a young woman with long, loose copper-blonde hair, a white robe slipping off her right shoulder, holding a few flowers.
tracks.what: Titian, Flora, about 1517, oil on canvas, 79.7 × 63.5 cm, inv. 1890 n. 1462 (page "D22" in the old numbering = map D23).
tracks.listen: The hair colour named after Titian, who she might be, and how she travelled from Amsterdam and Vienna to Florence.

tracks.section: First floor · Venice and the Verone
tracks.title: D26 · Veronese
tracks.where: Room D26, Veronese. Look for the tall canvas, about two and a half metres high, of a nobleman in a black fur-lined tunic with a sword, one glove off, his bare hand on the shoulder of his small son.
tracks.what: Paolo Caliari, known as Veronese, Portrait of Count Giuseppe da Porto with his son, Adriano, about 1555, oil on canvas, 247 × 133 cm, Contini Bonacossi no. 16 (page "D25" = map D26). Also: Veronese, Holy Family with Young St John and St Catherine, about 1565, oil on canvas, 86 × 122 cm (page "D26. Veronese Corridor" = map D27).
tracks.listen: How Veronese answered the Inquisition by changing a title, and a father's bare hand on his son's shoulder.

tracks.section: First floor · Venice and the Verone
tracks.title: D28 · The Verone
tracks.where: Room D28, the Verone: the long covered loggia at the river end of the first floor, with a row of statues. Look for the statue of the old Silenus cradling the infant Bacchus in his arms.
tracks.what: The Verone, the covered loggia on the Arno, with ancient and Renaissance statues, among them three monumental works from the Villa Medici in Rome. Jacopo del Duca, Silenus cradling Bacchus as a child, made between 1571 and 1574, a copy after a Roman original.
tracks.listen: A pause between two centuries, and an old companion of the wine god holding a baby.

tracks.title: E4 · Caravaggio's room
tracks.where: Room E4, Caravaggio – The Medusa, the first room off the corridor after the Verone. Find the wide canvas, about 1.35 metres across, of an angel seizing an old man's wrist as he is about to sacrifice a boy, with a calm hilly landscape behind. Guido Reni's tall David in a red feathered hat is in the same room.
tracks.what: Caravaggio, Sacrifice of Isaac, about 1603, oil on canvas, 104 × 135 cm, inv. 1890 no. 4659. Also: Guido Reni, David with the Head of Goliath, about 1605, oil on canvas, 222 × 147 cm. Artemisia Gentileschi's Judith and Caravaggio's Medusa are in this room (062, 063).
tracks.listen: Who Caravaggio was, the angel's grip that stops a sacrifice, and how a Caravaggio reached the Uffizi under someone else's name.

tracks.title: E4 · Caravaggio — Medusa
tracks.where: Room E4, Caravaggio – The Medusa. Look for the round painted shield with the severed head of Medusa, mouth wide open in a scream, snakes for hair and blood pouring from the neck.
tracks.what: Caravaggio, Medusa, 1595–1598, oil on canvas applied to a wooden shield (a parade shield), inv. 1890 no. 1351. No uffizi.it artwork page; placement from the October 2026 map, "E4 Caravaggio The Medusa".
tracks.listen: A shield that sat unattributed in the Medici armoury, rode on a wooden horse, and catches the instant between life and death.

tracks.title: E4 · Artemisia Gentileschi — Judith Beheading Holofernes
tracks.where: Room E4. Stand in front of the tall dark canvas, almost one and a half metres high, of two women holding a man down on a bed while one drives a sword into his neck, blood running onto the white sheets.
tracks.what: Artemisia Gentileschi, Judith Beheading Holofernes, about 1620, oil on canvas, 146.5 × 108 cm, inv. 1890 n. 1567 (page "D29" in the old numbering; the map puts Artemisia in E4).
tracks.listen: A painting that shocked Florence, the woman who painted it, and the fee she needed Galileo to collect.

tracks.title: E5 · Caravaggio — Bacchus
tracks.where: Room E5, Caravaggio – Il Bacco. Stand in front of the canvas, about a metre high, of a young man crowned with vine leaves who holds out a glass of red wine, with a bowl of fruit in front of him.
tracks.what: Caravaggio, Bacchus, about 1598, oil on canvas, 95 × 85 cm, inv. 1890 n. 5312 (page "D32" in the old numbering; the map says E5).
tracks.listen: A Caravaggio found in the storerooms, a god with dirty fingernails, and a tiny reflection in the carafe that no visitor can see.

tracks.title: E6 · Painting by candlelight
tracks.where: Room E6, Painting by Candlelight. Look for the wide night scene, about 1.3 metres across, of the Virgin, Joseph leaning on his stick and two angels bending over a manger, all lit by the newborn Child.
tracks.what: Gerrit van Honthorst, Adoration of the Child, about 1619–1620, oil on canvas, 95.5 × 131 cm, inv. 1890 no. 739.
tracks.listen: Gerard of the Nights, and a Nativity where the only light comes from the baby.

tracks.title: E7 · Rembrandt, Rubens and Van Dyck
tracks.where: Room E7, Rembrandt – Rubens – Van Dyck. Look for the canvas, just over a metre high, of an old bearded man, half-length, who seems lost in thought as he emerges from a dark background.
tracks.what: Rembrandt Harmenszoon van Rijn, Portrait of an old man (The Old Rabbi), 1665, oil on canvas, 104 × 86 cm, inv. 1890 no. 8435 (page "D34" in the old numbering; the map's E7 highlight).
tracks.listen: Rembrandt late in life, an old man he may have known from his own neighbourhood, and the two Flemish names on the door.

tracks.title: The way out
tracks.where: At the top of the Magliabechi staircase, where the route ends beyond Room E7, by the exit sign. There is a lift close by.
tracks.what: The end of the route. Down the Magliabechi staircase to the ground floor, past the cloakroom and the audioguide desk, and out by the back way out of the building, on the Palazzo Vecchio side.
tracks.listen: How to leave, and a last look back at a palace of offices that became one of the world's first public museums.
